      "observations": [
        "Fresh full seventeen-file compatibility patch read, including all changed SQL/test/manifest hunks. It bridges legacy message folders through server-key/parent/name traversal, adds a weak file-path cache alongside folder identity, initializes base-message URI and skips special/virtual folder setup under Panorama. It fills size/folder/view properties and single-message thread stubs. Historical Cc/recipients return empty success with TODOs; this is partial display compatibility, not a complete implementation.",
        "Review correctly distinguishes querying a Message-Id inside its folder from finding an arbitrary global Message-Id then rejecting another folder. The final assigned Git already binds folderId and messageId together, despite the older accepted-but-deferred discussion. Its fixed query retains both criteria. The adapter maps failed Message-Id lookup to NS_ERROR_ILLEGAL_VALUE. No uniqueness or deterministic choice among duplicate Message-Ids inside one folder is established.",
        "Changed tests verify the owning folder, reject a Message-Id present only in another folder, store messageSize and exercise both folder bridges. Their SQL fixture gives each message a distinct Message-Id, so they do not directly exercise the same Message-Id appearing in two folders. A focused proposed test is a duplicate Message-Id across folders with each owning DB returning its own key; this would test the exact review concern rather than only a missing-in-this-folder result. No test or SQL ran.",
        "Fixed APIs have evolved to numeric folder IDs and key-backed MessageDB getters; the existing focused bridge and current-header lessons are reused. Fixed size getters check 64-to-32-bit overflow, and Cc/recipients now delegate to MessageDB instead of returning the historical placeholder. View property getters obtain defaults then stored values. Weak cache lookup still concerns the folder file path rather than an asserted .msf filename. The temporary special/virtual folder skips remain at the fixed startup-pref gate. None of these checks proves complete migration, service lifetime or all display behavior."
